claims.text: Controlled aging will induce a dispersion of nanoscale precipitates in a high-entropy alloy.
A nanoscale precipitate dispersion produced by aging will improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
The starting alloy is as-cast or homogenized and has a primarily single-phase microstructure.
An optimized aging treatment can precipitate nanoscale oxide or intermetallic particles uniformly throughout the microstructure.
Temperatures from approximately 600°C to 800°C are representative of extreme structural-service environments.
The aging treatment will form a fine dispersion of nanoscale precipitates at grain boundaries.
The aging treatment will form a fine dispersion of nanoscale precipitates in intragranular regions.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin dislocations.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin grain boundaries.
Dislocation and grain-boundary pinning will restrict grain-boundary sliding and creep deformation at elevated temperatures.
Restricting elevated-temperature deformation will increase yield strength relative to the untreated state.
Restricting elevated-temperature deformation will reduce creep rate relative to the untreated state.
The aged microstructure will produce a statistically significant improvement in elevated-temperature yield strength relative to the same alloy in an as-cast or solution-treated condition.
The aged microstructure will produce a statistically significant improvement in creep resistance relative to the same alloy in an as-cast or solution-treated condition.
The predicted improvement is expected to hold between 600°C and 800°C in structural-application environments.
More aggressive corrosive environments or temperatures above 800°C may require additional alloy or process modifications.
